# Issue 96 assertion map

The source pin is `4fe5554` (`4fe5554c4c09ec522aae410afde6a298787a04a9`). This record starts with every observed assertion of `tests/config.test.sh` at that pin. Each parameter value has its own row. The unchanged shell test reports `212 cases; 0 failures` after Task 1.

Task 1 ports 165 assertions. Task 2 ports the remaining 47 assertions and both conditional guards, in the approved order. The complete shell test stays unchanged until Task 9. No assertion is omitted. The map stays as ignored plan evidence until the controller publishes the completed feature record.

Current host-case file locations: every earlier `tests/host-session.test.ts` replacement row resolves through [the complete 82-case relocation table](#approved-host-file-allocation-after-the-actual-standalone-cutoff). That table gives the current file for each name. The shared managed/hosts/resumeArgs/saved helper is now `tests/lib/host-session-fixture.ts`.

For each invalid reader case, the new test checks a `ConfigError`, field diagnostic, CLI status 2, empty stdout, and the selected file. For each valid table case, it checks the typed result and exact CLI JSON, final newline, and empty stderr. The separate message rows below require exact diagnostic text. Literal strings keep their parsed bytes. Worktree setup stays data during reads.

The gate regression in `tests/verify.test.sh`, case `faults`, adds a type error in `tests/lib/bad.ts`. With the old scripts-only compiler scope, it fails with `tsc does not name tests/lib/bad.ts`. With `tsconfig.runtime.json`, it passes. The runtime compiler scope includes scripts and Bun tests. Native Claude tests keep their separate host environment for the later hook conversion; they are excluded from this Bun scope.

The product-preload case checks valid and invalid config, then proves the preload can run without the isolation config flag. The global-file case keeps a private global bunfig present during valid and invalid startup. On Bun 1.4.2, an implicit global runtime preload does not run; an explicit `--preload` control does run. This test does not claim that Bun runtime starts implicitly read global bunfig. The [Bun configuration reference](https://bun.com/docs/runtime/bunfig#global-vs-local) limits global bunfig to package-manager commands. Macro, environment-file, shadow-executable, auto-install, cache, and crash-report cases have separate assertions.


## Task 2 runtime boundary

The controller approved this runtime change. The isolated Bun shebang starts before launcher code. Missing, broken, or nonexecutable Bun therefore returns the native env or kernel result. The macOS fixture results are 127, 1, and 126, respectively. No discovery, config payload, or command dispatch starts. The cost is a native diagnostic for an absent runtime instead of the old Bash-owned Celetis status-2 message. An executable Bun below 1.4.2 still returns the Celetis status-2 diagnostic before discovery. Linux kernel execution is UNRUN in this task.

The complete launcher shebang runs with BSD `/usr/bin/env` and GNU `genv` on macOS. The same portable test uses `env` on Linux. The line includes cache/crash-report assignments, no environment file, no install, a null config, and no macros. A selected Bun path with spaces passes too. The fixture uses quoted `\_` for a space because quotes around a literal space fail in a macOS shebang.

## Task 2 process replacement and final checks

The old launcher uses exec and keeps its PID. Task 2 uses process.execve with process.execPath, the isolated Bun arguments, and the child environment. The copied-launcher PID/SIGKILL regression first found different PIDs and a surviving installed command. The final test proves the same PID and no survivor. The inherited stdin and HUP/INT/TERM cases also pass. No launcher parent or supervisor remains after dispatch.

The Bun 1.4.2 runtime exposes process.execve on the tested macOS host. The private PID test proves that it replaces the process. The source fails if this required API is unavailable; it has no alternate dispatch path. Linux kernel execution remains UNRUN. The portable PID and signal cases remain in the test file for final Linux CI.

Final focused evidence is in the Task 2 report. It includes all 71 launcher/build cases and the 174 affected foundation cases. The complete generated shebang is checked with BSD env and GNU env 9.12. Fresh native fixture programs have explicit readiness checks before the test measures launcher behavior. This does not change the production 10-second request deadlines.


## Task 2 review fix 1

The app-server cleanup now retains the first interruption and checks it after the server exits. Three cases send SIGHUP, SIGINT, or SIGTERM only after the server receives cleanup TERM. Each sends a later different signal too. They require the first signal status, server removal, and no command dispatch. The existing pending-reply signal case remains.

The obsolete nativePath/cygpath converter and its positive compatibility test are removed. This follows the controller ruling and the Bun/macOS/Linux scope. The two mainCheckout Windows Git-output cases remain as path-data cases; they do not execute a converter. All native installation checks remain. The original conversion assertion has its removed-dependency explanation above.

Task 3 controller ruling: an explicit profile with `reviewer.effort: ["medium"]` violates the published string schema. The old jq program accepts that subarray by accident. `array-valued reviewer effort fails the published profile schema` checks the old acceptance and the new status-2 rejection separately. Malformed array-valued profiles now fail. Valid profiles are unchanged. This is the only added schema divergence.

The resolver catches failure only around its ps query. As in the source, a failed query gives an unowned lock. The controlled failed-query test checks normal resolution with empty stderr. The separate real-process oracle keeps actual ps inspection of a private land.ts child.

## Task 3 review fix 1: numeric boundaries

Controller ruling: scorer numeric input must be a JavaScript safe integer before scoring and schema-1 serialization. Bias is 0 through 9007199254740991, inclusive. Attempt is 1 through 9007199254740991, inclusive. CAP_EFFORT_BIAS has the same range as --bias. Explicit --bias still overrides the environment. Values above this bound now fail even when Bash accepted them. Bash overflow, rounded numeric fields, Infinity, and null output fields are not preserved. The reported attempt overflow, which Bash rejects, again returns status 2. Normal arithmetic and the digit range 0 through 2 do not change.

Task 9 documentation switch: add these exact ranges to the public scorer flags, environment input, and schema-1 descriptions in docs/capability.md. Keep existing field-specific diagnostic text. A valid attempt of 4 or greater still returns STOP before host, config, profile, or runtime lookup. An invalid numeric input fails before any such lookup and emits no stdout.

| --attempt 9007199254740991 | Exact attempt field and STOP line; no lookup even with invalid host, config, and profiles | Ported, fix 1 |

## Task 4: worktrees and TypeScript setup

The source pin for every row below is `4fe5554c4c09ec522aae410afde6a298787a04a9`. The old worktree and setup programs and both old test files are unchanged working references. All product work uses private fixture repositories. No product setup, host session, remote issue, push to a real remote, runner, or landing was used.

The TypeScript replacements retain real Git repositories, real local bare origins, real Git hooks, and a real setup signal oracle. `tests/lib/lane-fixture.ts` gives each case private mutable state, a checked Git helper, and REST-only gh fixtures. Each command call also checks that its private temporary directory is empty on exit. Test concurrency is bounded at 24. File timings and raw logs are in `.superpowers/sdd/96/task-4-report.md`.

### Declared language and stream changes

| Old assertion or interface | Replacement | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bash setup functions, `$1`, `$PWD`, and `$BASH_EXECUTION_STRING` | TypeScript local state and functions, `process.argv[2]`, `process.cwd()`, and `readFileSync(import.meta.path)` | The approved setup language changed. Equivalent fixture actions record cwd/main/state and exact source bytes; no shell program runs inside TypeScript. |
| Setup stdout is redirected to stderr | Setup inherits stdin, stdout, and stderr without interception | Explicit #96 stream change. stderr remains exact; stdout data stays on stdout. |
| Path-only stdout after nonempty setup | The command adds one LF before its final absolute path line | Controller ruling: inherited setup output may end without an LF. A separator keeps the final path record complete. Executed nonempty, empty, omitted, marked, failed try, and preparation-failed try cases pin exact stdout bytes. `setup lane` adds no path record. |
| Bash `set -e` implicit external failure | Each TypeScript fixture checks `exitCode` before it continues or exits | Explicit Bun execution contract. Checked-external-failure cases return the external status from try and retain worktree failure cleanup. |
| Old Bash text | Non-executed rejection data in `new setup cleanup: old Bash is rejected` | No conversion or Bash fallback exists. |
| `confignobun`, `confignobunread`, `setupnobun` | `selected Bun: product PATH bun cannot replace the active reader or setup runtime` | Celetis already runs on the selected Bun. Shadowing a different `bun` on product PATH no longer changes the in-process reader or selected setup runtime. The old missing-Bun wrapper failures are obsolete. New and existing config planning still round-trips before product writes. |
| `.sh` sourced worktree interface | Direct exports from `scripts/lib/worktree.ts` | Removed Bash sourcing interface. `markerOf`, `runSetup`, `worktrees`, `checkoutOf`, `removeCheckout`, and `removeLane` are shared typed operations. |

The private mode-0600 `.ts` source is outside both canonical checkout roots. The guards run before any source write and reject TMPDIR in main, in the lane, and a symlink into the lane. A real SIGTERM case checks forwarding, status 143 even when setup handles the signal with exit 0, cleanup, and no marker. Startup isolation is checked with real product `.env` and `bunfig.toml` poison files and an explicit absolute import from each checkout.

### Additional Task 4 contract cases

| Contract | Typed evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Zero final line breaks | Worktree stdin/source case with ending length 0; setup2 block bytes; try stdin/source case with ending length 0 |
| One final line break | Worktree stdin/source case with ending length 1; setup1 block bytes; try stdin/source case with ending length 1 |
| Three final line breaks | Worktree stdin/source case with ending length 3; setup3 block bytes; try stdin/source case with ending length 3 |
| Syntax failure | Worktree new-branch cleanup and existing-checkout retention; try returns 1 and keeps path |
| Uncaught exception | Worktree new-branch cleanup and existing-checkout retention; try returns 1 and keeps path |
| Explicit `process.exit(7)` | Worktree failure returns 1, creates no marker, deletes only new state; try returns 7 and keeps path |
| Checked external failure | Worktree cleanup/retention and try status 9; every external command in fixture setup code has its status checked |
| No Bash conversion | Old Bash data fails as TypeScript; no Bash child, helper, or fallback is used |
| Setup preparation failure | try retains its final path line, a detached clean checkout, and no marker |
| Unsafe temporary directories | Lane TMPDIR, main TMPDIR, and TMPDIR symlink into lane fail before setup text is written |
| Signal and cleanup | Real private setup child handles SIGTERM; runSetup returns 143, removes source directory, and leaves no marker |
| Startup isolation | Real `.env` and Bun preload poison files remain inactive; explicit absolute lane and main imports succeed |
| Every command exit | Fixture call() asserts its private temporary directory is empty after success or failure |

Task 4 fixture corrections against the old reference: `removal` deletes `prototype/1-alt` before it reaches the dirty `prototype/1-probe-ui` checkout. The typed dirty-prototype assertion therefore checks the same protected lane, dirty checkout, branch, and remote state as the old case; it does not require an earlier independent prototype to survive. `settingsrecorded` intentionally changes no product file on its rerun. The typed rerun checks a clean tree instead of attempting a no-op commit. The original status checks for raw Git removal failures remain nonzero rather than forcing status 1; setup outside Git explicitly preserves status 1.

### Native checkout identity check

`worktrees()` normalizes each Git path with native `resolve`. The commands normalize Git checkout roots the same way, and setup lane membership uses native `relative` plus the registered worktree list. Existing symlink write refusals and the canonical temporary-path guard stay intact. Two additional tests first failed when a real Git wrapper returned an equivalent `/.` path: main-branch setup was incorrectly allowed, and a registered lane was incorrectly refused. Both now pass. The fixture runs real private Git before it changes only the returned path spelling, checks the real status, and keeps real marker/status oracles. This is local path identity evidence. Windows and MSYS runtime acceptance remain UNRUN; no compatibility path was added.

After this change, the scoped path/ownership/temp rerun passes 22 cases in 6.60 s. The final staged gate is `.superpowers/sdd/96/task-4-gate-final.log`. The complete focused files passed 47 and 109 cases before the two added identity cases; the new cases and the affected identity callers were then rerun. No full suite ran.

### Task 4 fix 1: complete restored assertion sets

Review found four incomplete old oracles in the initial port. The source rows above now point to their complete restored checks. The handwired case compares the entire ownership record and excludes store ownership. Closed-issue refusal checks run before the next mutation and include both local and origin refs. Final success checks include origin prototype removal. The setup stderr payload has an exact complete-line check, and the open-issue/no-PR case checks both required diagnostic parts.

Only `tests/setup.test.ts` and `tests/worktree.test.ts` changed. The current production source passes every restored check. No production change or artificial RED mutation was used. The scoped worktree run passes 3 cases in 3.46 s; the handwired setup run passes 1 case in 1.99 s. Raw logs are `.superpowers/sdd/96/task-4-fix-1-worktree.log` and `.superpowers/sdd/96/task-4-fix-1-setup.log`. The required staged gate is recorded in `.superpowers/sdd/96/task-4-fix-1-gate.log`. No full suite, helper rerun, or live check was run in this fix.


## Task 5: Runner, sessions and advisory update locks

The source baseline is `4fe5554`. The new runner uses `scripts/celetis-flow.ts` and the new resolver recognizes `land.ts`. The old `.sh` and `.pl` entrypoints stay as internal comparison references until Task 9. No new runtime calls an old entrypoint.

`validateSession` is the one typed record validator. `readSession`, `writeSession` and `selectSavedSession` use it. The launcher uses `selectSavedSession` and `serializeSession` before discovery, then the runner checks the same sorted snapshot after discovery. The saved host and UUID control Resume. The runner takes only the issue lock for Resume; it takes no automatic runner lock, starts no watcher and performs no refresh.

`UpdateLock` binds the system `flock(2)` through `bun:ffi`. Each child receives the same open file description as descriptor 3. `installedRoot` and `codexRequest` pass it to their nested host commands. Cleanup sends TERM, waits one second, sends KILL to the real command process group, waits for exit, and closes the parent's descriptor. It never explicitly unlocks. The per-host file remains `celetis-update.lock`; the monotonic total deadline remains 120 seconds, including lock wait, with 50 ms polls. Identity discovery keeps 60 seconds, and the herdr working/blocked wait keeps `--timeout 5000`.

### Expanded parameter inventory

| Baseline case | Each retained parameter | Typed evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| saved_status | Claude idle; Claude working; Claude unknown; Codex done; Codex blocked | Five named session cases save the exact record and resume the exact UUID. |
| valid_pane | Claude w1:p1; Claude w1:pE; Claude wa0:pz9; Codex wW:p14; Codex wW:pE | Five named cases pin the pane argument. |
| launch | Claude and Codex, each with triage, feature, bug, chore, hotfix, plan and implement | Fourteen full argv/cwd/stdin/record assertions. Feature records specify. |
| exact_resume | Claude triage, bug, hotfix and implement; Codex feature, chore and plan | Seven exact saved-host invocations; no watcher or refresh. |
| per-host session cases | Claude and Codex: prior host, old saved turn, recovery, old pane identity, startup exit and project default | Each host has its own named case. |
| outside_herdr | Claude and Codex, each with HERDR_ENV unset, empty and 0 | Six named cases require no herdr call and a null saved identity. |
| invalid_panes | Both hosts, each with unset, empty, invalid, w:p1, w1:p, w1:t1, w1:p1:extra, -w1:p1, leading space, trailing space, slash suffix, LF suffix and tab suffix | Each value fails before host, update or herdr calls. |
| shared identity failures | Both hosts: no-save, unsaved-blocked, unsaved-unknown, foreign-checkout and wrong-host | Ten named startup/refused-resume cases. |
| Claude identity failures | no-id; stale-id; wrong-session-host; malformed-identity; invalid-status | Five named startup/refused-resume cases. |
| Codex identity failures | bad-id; bad-json; wrong-kind; missing-status | Four named startup/refused-resume cases. |
| replaced_record | Host changes to Claude; UUID changes to 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 | Two valid replacement records fail the frozen snapshot check before launch. |
| bad_records | schema 0; other host; feature step; issue 8; string issue; foreign checkout; --last ID; numeric ID; extra key; missing schema; schema-only root; empty object; array; invalid JSON; schema 1 with other host | The shared validator refuses every input. |
| Codex persistence | Wrong saved ID; ephemeral thread | Both leave the starting record with null identity. |
| launcher_resume | YAML/Git defaults Claude and Codex with no Claude executable; explicit conflicting host | The saved Codex UUID controls discovery and launch. Explicit conflicts fail. |
| config/usage | Missing config; invalid landing; second-session config change; abc, 0, 7x, #, 7 abc, -h, --open, --board 7, 7 --board, --resume, --resume abc, --resume 7 8 and 7 --resume | Exact usage/status plus no-effect assertions. |
| update phase failures | Marketplace; plugin update; installed-root list | Each command, status, cause, sequence, absent session and released issue lock is checked. |
| update_hang | Marketplace; plugin update; installed-root list | A test clock advances the real 120-second supervisor. Real TERM-ignoring children and descendants must stop. A separate real 400 ms timeout checks the runtime timer. |
| codex_lookup | Timeout; interruption | Real RPC children and descendants stop. The original stderr appears once. Private temporary files and both lock types are checked. |
| shared_lock | Two repositories; helper SIGKILL with a surviving command | Both full runners and direct updater helpers prove that updates do not overlap. |
| stale owner | Issue and automatic refs, with Claude/Codex contenders; dead PID; reused PID; wrong executable; malformed owner; replacement owner; zombie session | Real Git compare-and-swap and real process identity checks. The zombie test stops a private Bun parent while its child exits. |
| lifecycle idle | Both hosts: idle and done; working, blocked, unknown, missing status, ready, other host, null identity, wrong identity host, name kind and wrong UUID | Each reply is independently checked. |
| late and after_wait | Claude blocked; Codex unknown | Final resolver and identity checks prevent /exit after state changes. |
| saved lifecycle | Both hosts, each blocked and unknown | The verified first turn stays open and keeps the issue lock. |
| lifecycle resume/update/handoff | Both hosts; update success and failure | Exact update commands and saved session counts remain pinned. |
| guards | Claude unchanged; Claude dirty; Codex live landing; Codex removed resolver | Real resolver decisions keep the foreground open. The live landing uses land.ts. |
| endings | Claude idle accepted; Claude done failed; Codex idle failed; Codex done accepted | One /exit attempt never advances before actual foreground exit. |
| signals | Baseline Codex TERM plus added INT and HUP; all three updater signals | The runner waits for foreground exit; updater cleanup keeps status 1 and completes in less than five seconds. |
| registration | Claude issue mode; Codex automatic mode | Real parent SIGKILL before Git registration starts no host. After registration, the orphan host holds all applicable refs until it exits. |
| crash | Claude exit 23 | The failure remains a recovery error and writes no no-progress row. |
| herdr flow | Bug-to-plan plus a second issue; feature with and without a spec; open epic; closed wontfix; live landing | Tab names, repeated resolver calls, exact prompt/wait arrays, issue line, no-progress rows and the 5000 ms wait stay covered. |
| automatic scheduling | Ordered issues; no auto gate; GitHub list failure; per-issue failure; dirty main; locked issue; obsolete Git gates; YAML bug/specify auto gates | Named cases use private clocks for repeated 60-second waits. stdin stays with the foreground host. |
| board | Contract 1; all baseline issue rows; main and lane dirtiness; stuck row; live issue and runner refs; both defaults; missing other host; GitHub failure | The real board contract checker and exact metadata/precedence/list/flow assertions run against the produced JSON. |

### Path callers and test helpers

| Old path or caller | Current typed caller | Cutover state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| scripts/celetis-flow.sh | scripts/celetis-flow.ts | Old reference stays until Task 9. |
| scripts/plugin-update.pl | scripts/plugin-update.ts and scripts/lib/update-lock.ts | Real FFI and inherited descriptors replace the Perl supervisor. No helper interpreter or native binary ships. |
| scripts/lib/session.sh | scripts/lib/session.ts | Record, observation, persistence, host arguments and startup diagnostics have one typed implementation. |

| scripts/lib/host.ts installedRoot/codexRequest | Optional inherited descriptor in the existing operations | Existing catalog and RPC validation retained; the nested command keeps the advisory lock. Descriptor-bound Claude stderr goes straight to the updater capture file. |
| scripts/lib/process.ts run | Argument-array input and inherited-descriptor options | Git blob/transaction stdin and nested host output use the shared process helper. |
| tests/lib/pool.sh runner/session uses | tests/lib/runner-fixture.ts | Eight private cases run at once through a fair FIFO queue. Fixtures are TypeScript programs. Each case cleans up its processes and scratch state. |
| Shell wait versus captured pipe EOF | Separate exited and result promises | SIGKILL tests wait for process exit before releasing a blocked Git stub or finishing a live foreground. Pipe close remains separate and occurs after inherited writers exit. |
| A file-wide per-test child cleanup | afterAll fallback in runner-lock.test.ts, plus per-case cleanup | A completed concurrent case cannot kill another case's live supervisor. Cleanup only signals child objects that are still running. |
| Old fixture sleep/Perl clock stubs | Private TypeScript clock wrappers | Production deadlines remain unchanged. Real processes, real advisory locks, Git refs, ps state and exit codes remain the oracles. |
| Existing lane config fixture | A committed lane config before runner start | The typed resolver correctly rejected the first uncommitted fixture as dirty. The corrected case matches the baseline committed lane. |

The old helper polling ceilings are test bounds, not product operation deadlines. The private managed-runner wrapper restores the old sleep stub: a 1000 ms watcher poll uses 50 ms. It does not change the 60-second identity deadline, the 5000 ms herdr timeout, or any update supervisor clock. Typed fixture condition waits fail after ten seconds (the baseline lifecycle helper permits 30 seconds); each test has a 25-second bound, and each file must finish within 30 seconds. Process-start identity, update timeout and signal cleanup are never replaced by synthetic liveness replies, except the two stale-owner contender barriers that deliberately coordinate a missing PID. Live and zombie ownership still use actual ps results.

Linux runtime acceptance is UNRUN on this macOS host. Live host sessions and real plugin refresh are UNRUN under the user's live-check waiver. The macOS FFI decision point uses Bun 1.4.2 (744846f84), with authorized process inspection after the sandbox denied ps. The task report stores the final command logs and exact file times.

### Task 5 review fix 1

The initial close-time replacement used a truthiness check. It did not preserve baseline `tests/celetis-flow.test.sh:928`. The restored board case reads `issue-4.json.closed_at` and compares `closedAt` with that exact string. The row above now names the actual check.

Descriptor capture also has two new real-process overflow cases in `tests/process.test.ts`. Each child writes again after TERM. Instrumented reads of the retained-string byte counts must stay at or below the configured limit, and returned text must end on a complete UTF-8 character. The stdout case checks the existing maxBuffer error fallback; the stderr case keeps the captured child error text. A split-UTF-8 success case covers the descriptor path below the limit.

The controller ruled that the hard 30-second file limit takes precedence over the single-file allocation after two fixture optimizations did not meet it. Private repositories use a real bare origin, real commits, real worktrees and raw GitHub argv logs. The only GitHub operations are private stub replies. Production poll constants stay at 60 polls and 15,000 ms; the private entry wrapper records the unchanged requested duration and resolves its sleep at once.

### Final allocation and exact-owner check

The controller first approved two entries at attempt 1 with the unchanged inherit/max pair. A PR-file time spread from 24.01 s to 32.51 s had no safe margin, so the controller approved a third entry for checks/reruns. Task 9 must discover `tests/land.test.ts`, `tests/land-pr.test.ts` and `tests/land-checks.test.ts`. The shared helper creates one private template context per entry, so the entries do not share mutable state when CI discovers them. The scheduling sort, the twelve-case experiment, and shared Git clone experiment were removed. Ordinary cases use real Git directly. The Git wrapper is used only for the injected errors and the raw-Git evidence case.

The two baseline merge rejection blocks are `tests/land.test.sh:853–865` and `:895–906`. They check the failed merge status, the message and kept refs; they do not call the baseline zero-merge refusal helper. Their typed replacements require exactly one attempted merge request. Every ordinary refusal still requires zero.

Baseline `tests/land.test.sh:199` rejects a Bash runtime diagnostic. The Bash-specific path/line text is obsolete under #96. The shared typed `land` helper replaces that check with a rejection of unexpected runtime stack frames. Existing status, output and ref assertions remain.

The PID-file ownership comparison retains Bash command substitution's exact bytes: only final LF characters are removed. A different PID and the current PID followed by a space must both stay. The space case first failed with ENOENT after `trimEnd()` removed its lock. The one-line `.replace(/\n+$/, '')` fix now retains both exact replacement values. Raw RED evidence is `.superpowers/sdd/96/task-6-lock-red.log`.

### Stream preservation

The first stream warning case ran RED before the boundary fix: one failure, zero passes, 17 expectations, 2.02 s. It expected seven exact ordinary-call warning lines and received an empty list. The controller ruled that restoring these warnings preserves the old stream contract and adds no feature. The typed Git and GitHub boundaries now write successful ordinary-call stderr. The explicit quiet boundaries stay quiet: merge-tree, green polling, re-run completion polling, pull-main fetch/merge, captured parent/sub-issue reads and the captured branch-delete request. Failure stderr is emitted once. The existing GitHub unavailable and rerun-refusal cases now require exactly one HTTP 502 diagnostic. No production constant changed.

The old single-file timing records are 43.99 s (121 pass, four known fixture/process-access failures), 28.47 s (125 pass), 37.95 s (126 pass), 38.26 s (126 pass) and 31.18 s (126 pass with the reverted twelve-case experiment). The two-file records are merge 7.64 s and PR 24.01 s, then merge 12.05 s and PR 32.51 s. These earlier allocations are not the final time-limit proof. The task report stores the final three separate commands and times.

Final Task 6 proof: `tests/land.test.ts` passes 42 cases in 8.33 s; `tests/land-pr.test.ts` passes 49 cases in 15.05 s; `tests/land-checks.test.ts` passes 36 cases in 15.70 s. Total: 127 cases and 2,556 expectations. The final staged gate ends `verify: PASS`. The stream fixture first supplied an existing PR while expecting a create warning; the corrected fixture starts with no PR. The name manifest keeps all 126 earlier names and adds only the stream case. Full command, raw-argv and real-ref evidence is in `.superpowers/sdd/96/task-6-report.md`.

## Task 7 — board port (baseline `4fe5554`)

The source pin is `4fe5554c4c09ec522aae410afde6a298787a04a9`. The complete test source was ported before any production edit. All exact equality, status, body, negative execution, and no-write assertions stay. Browser URLs stay `board.js`, `view.mjs`, `ui.mjs`, `panel.mjs`, and `palette.mjs`; these files become generated output. The internal old modules and shell adapter stay operational until Task 9.

The Node support partitions (accepted: `22.18.0`, `22.23.3`, `24.2.0`, `25.0.0`, `26.8.2`; refused: `18.20.4`, `20.19.0`, `22.17.1`, `23.11.0`, `24.1.0`) and the Node diagnostic are removed under #96. New Bun partitions accept `1.4.2`, `1.4.3`, `1.5.0`, `2.0.0` and refuse `1.4.1`, `1.3.99`, `0.9.0`. A real CLI process with Bun `1.4.1` must print the exact floor refusal before invalid argv, a stdin read failure, Git or any producer. Package engine/bin and shebang assertions now require Bun `>=1.4.2` and `cli.ts`. The adapter starts the selected Bun through `process.execPath`, so the old no-Node error is obsolete; an isolated PATH without a Bun executable must still work.

### Expanded parameter inventory before production edits

The full arrays and nested loops remain in the typed tests. Their expanded input sets are:

- Config root JSON text: empty, whitespace, `{`, `{}{}`, malformed data; root values `null`, `[]`, `true`, `7`, `"text"`. List keys are `data`, `run`, `resume`; supplied values are `null`, string, empty list, and mixed list. Control arguments cover every code point 0 through 31 and 127 for each key (99 inputs), plus each direct/tab-link/DEL-link path for each key (9 inputs). Executable boundaries cross each key with absolute, parent segment, missing, directory, mode, external-link, direct-lane and lane-link (24 inputs). Data braces: `{n}`, `{agent}`, `{step}`, `x{n}`, `{`, `}`. Run/Resume braces cross each key with `x{n}`, `{n}x`, `{step}`, `{`, `}` (10 inputs), plus missing-number and Resume agent refusals. Ports: accepted 1024 and 65535; refused 1023, 65536, 4403.5, string 4403, null, true, false. All 37 named REFUSALS are retained.
- CLI config forms cross `--config-stdin` and `check --config-stdin` with all six checkout failures (12 inputs), 25 invalid JSON/schema inputs (50 inputs), 10 executable/security failures (20 inputs), read failure (2 inputs), and EOF chunking (2 inputs). Public argv keeps all 19 refusal tuples. Path starts cover main, main subfolder, and a symlink. Port fallbacks cover absent, nonnumeric and zero PORT at configured and default ports (6 inputs), explicit PORT override, occupied PORT, configured listen, invalid PORT and nonloopback refusal. Producer results cover valid, stderr failure, stdout failure, silent failure, invalid JSON and invalid contract document.
- Contract: each RULES mutation keeps its named rule index, original field and exact place assertion; duplicate lanes/stages, invalid JSON, other-contract handling, absent/null/unknown optional fields, and all agent/default mutations stay.
- Placement: every RULES tuple, each herdr status (including inherited object keys), per-key capability cross products, press timeout/busy transitions, and all priority/order cases stay.
- View: both flow and null Run hints, notice/state variants, each pipeline/search/path case, and the existing exact value assertions stay.
- Server: every data failure tuple, command-specific absence tuple, simultaneous press pair, herdr error and unsafe-id tuple, HTTP REFUSED tuple, static asset tuple, default-change body tuple, and agent trust tuple stay. Explicit Run agents are `nope`, `Claude`, `a-b`, empty, object, 123, shell text, unavailable, unknown-effective, null-default and unavailable-default; every refusal retains zero terminal commands. The complete literal tuple tables remain in `board/server.test.ts`.
- Adapter executable kinds: external, lane, missing, mode, directory, each with status 1, config diagnostic and no producer. Adapter invalid input: `{`, unknown field, empty data, missing-number Run agent, Resume agent, port zero. Main YAML cases: missing, invalid, unknown. Lane cases: lane root and lane subfolder. Repository default gates explicitly cover triage, specify, bug, chore, hotfix, plan, implement.
- Agent integration: default Claude Run #6, explicit Claude under Codex default #7, default Codex #8, saved Codex Resume #8 under changed Claude YAML, unavailable Codex and unknown Run/default refusals, with exact YAML/Git/call snapshots throughout.

Actual Chromium at desktop width and 375×812, native desktop selection, and a real herdr terminal boundary are **UNRUN** under the user instruction to ignore live checks. Current CLI help and deterministic fixture argv prove no live terminal acceptance.

### Task 7 delivery and interim caller check

- `scripts/board.ts` uses the shared Celetis YAML reader only for the adapter. `board/config.ts` independently validates stdin JSON, paths and executable modes. The board package imports no Celetis host/session/YAML implementation.
- The adapter uses `process.execPath` and the fixed `data`, selected-agent `run`, saved-host `resume`, and port lists. `scripts/lib/session.ts` remains the sole saved-session validator. No validator was copied. Launcher and runner keep `CELETIS_RESUME_RECORD`.
- `scripts/build.ts` compiles all six delivery targets before it writes any output. A missing browser source and a browser syntax error each first failed their no-partial-output oracle; both now pass. Browser assets alone were copied from the private output. The public copied launcher stays byte-for-byte unchanged.
- `scripts/verify.sh` has exact generated roles for `board/board.js`, `board/view.mjs`, `board/ui.mjs`, `board/panel.mjs`, and `board/palette.mjs`. It checks their syntax and fresh generated bytes, and runs the strict board TypeScript config. These five generated files are not formatted by Biome. All authored TypeScript remains checked; only adversarial board test fixtures share the existing test-only any rule.
- The three shell board fixture programs are replaced by executable `.ts` sources. Old runtime entrypoints remain internal references until Task 9. Task 9 removes their old `.mjs`/shell test callers and discovers all 13 board/adapter `.test.ts` entries listed above; it also keeps `tests/build.test.ts`.
- The late self-review restored the optional DOM method calls in the browser source and made `Action.id` explicit. Type-erased source comparison shows only formatting, equivalent DOM coercion/defaults, and equivalent typed filter callbacks. HTML, CSS, font bytes, storage keys, and UI copy are unchanged.

Task 7 final cleanup proof: the agent fixture records each private detached pane group, kills each owned group in `finally`, and verifies all four groups are absent before removing its private directory. The last focused run passes its one existing case with 12 expectations in 8.91 s. The case-to-entry allocation stays at 296. The cleanup edit was staged before the final gate, which ends `verify: PASS`. The raw result is `.superpowers/sdd/96/task-7-agent-cleanup-final.log`.

## Task 8: native sources and manual checks

The source pin remains `4fe5554`. Task 8 uses Bun for the test entries and assertions. The hook keeps its native `register(on)` interface. The production source and generated module exports have separate identities. The live native module-loading check (V6) and token-using manual checks are **UNRUN** under the user instruction `ignore live checks`. Deterministic tests are not native-host acceptance.

The complete initial port ran RED before the hook and manual program edits. Its native entry source selector had a name collision and used the generated export twice. The observer source selector did fail on its absent source. The name collision was found by strict type checking and fixed. The later GREEN logs cover all 70 entry cases in each requested module and all six observer cases in each requested module. No source RED is claimed for the 70 entry cases. Public command rejection checks and signal/launch-status tests were added during self-review; their order is in the task report.

| tests/native-entry.test.sh:4 | The test-kit command is replaced by \`bun test tests/native-entry.test.ts\`; 70 original cases run for each actual export. |
| tests/native-observer.test.sh:6–8 | The copied test-kit source is removed. \`tests/native-observer.test.ts\` owns all six original assertions sets for both module exports. The test uses Bun and the real \`register\`. |
| custom-part-harness obsolete_option | \`tests/custom-part-program.test.ts\`: \`--mcp-config obsolete\` returns 2, prints usage, and does not call the host. |
| custom-part-harness no_transition_run | \`tests/custom-part-program.test.ts\`: an absent native transition returns 2, names the exact scenario, and writes status 2 in the saved artifact. |
| custom-part-harness client_exit_run | \`tests/custom-part-program.test.ts\`: client status 7 returns 2; exact error; five generated files; saved status 7; valid result text remains in the stream. |
| custom-part-harness evidence_checks | \`tests/custom-part-program.test.ts\`: both valid and checker-failure runs keep 97 generated files, 24 streams, version, exact input fields, source strings, hashes, and restrictions. Unrelated lookalike files are excluded. |
| custom-part-harness evidence_checks native worktree | The saved worktree input has two ordered user messages, unchanged recording instruction, and the exact guide invocation. Both completed result rows keep the same session ID. |
| manual-harness product_context host=claude,codex folder=.,area/sub | \`tests/manual-harness.test.ts\`: 25 received prompts plus saved context; root-to-leaf instruction order; excludes physical ancestors and unrelated folders; exact source paths, snapshot bytes, hashes, case-13 format and case-20 form. |
| manual-harness linked_checkout | \`tests/manual-harness.test.ts\`: real linked checkout fixture uses its own AGENTS.md and excludes the parent root and outside instructions. |
| manual-harness empty_context | \`tests/manual-harness.test.ts\`: empty source array and explicit no-instruction message. |
| manual-harness unreadable_instructions host=claude,codex | \`tests/manual-harness.test.ts\`: instruction read error stops before any host call; exact diagnostic is retained. |
| manual-harness completed_reconnect | \`tests/manual-step-checks.test.ts\` and public manual harness: completed reconnect gives one recovered service event and the exact WARN line. |
| manual-harness two_failed_checks | \`tests/manual-step-checks.test.ts\` and public manual harness: exact ordered list of the missing Fallback and Issue form fields. |
| manual custom-part setup guard | \`evaluateCustom\` rejects setupFound and forbidden setup markers. The setup fixture text is TypeScript data. It never runs during native entry. |

### Self-review guards

The extra guards reject trailing space and CR characters in a client status, keep trailing space significant in an exact stop, and preserve a trailing space in a Git checkout path. Signal tests cover SIGINT and SIGTERM in both manual programs. Launch tests cover missing and nonexecutable hosts. These guards have separate RED and GREEN logs in the report.

A further replay guard keeps string user message content valid, as the old optional jq traversal did. It has a separate RED log and full-file GREEN checks.

### Task 8 review fix 1

The observer test converts both URL values with `fileURLToPath`. Its root still has no trailing separator. The added case `observer contracts preserve filesystem paths in a spaced checkout` copies only the observer entry, native host helper, and both observer modules into private scratch. It runs only `compact observation`, so it cannot invoke itself. RED records one failed regression with both copied module cases failing. GREEN records 13 passes for the full observer entry and two passes for the separate spaced-checkout proof. The native hook and generated output did not change.

The current inventory has 651 case-to-entry pairs. Only the affected observer entry and the separate spaced proof were rerun in fix 1. The other selected logs remain the prior passing evidence. The original source-RED gap and live waiver remain unchanged.

### Task 9 obsolete language diagnostics

The historical shfmt, ShellCheck, Bash syntax, Node syntax, jq syntax and Perl syntax diagnostic bytes are obsolete with those program languages. The gate now rejects their tracked extensions and extensionless interpreter declarations. Negative classifier cases explicitly cover shell, Perl, jq and Node declarations and .sh/.pl/.jq/authored-.mjs paths. TypeScript Biome parse/lint/format and strict runtime/browser/native failures retain the refusal and named child-failure obligations. Version drift keeps its exact warning contract using the surviving native actionlint pin. Each affected assertion row has this disposition in the machine-readable record.

### Task 9 runtime binding permission boundary

`board/runtime.test.ts`: runtime binding preserves an execute-only native command without a read permission condition. The pinned Bun 1.4.2 macOS realpath incompatibility on an execute-only file is unresolved, with exact Node and Bun evidence in the task report; no native compatibility PASS is claimed from Bun's refusal.

The current macOS verifier independently reproduces the same auto failure. The 50 other automatic files and both nine-entry process subsets pass at that base. These are retained RED facts; the earlier isolated auto PASS is not closure.

The real Codex herdr reply is delayed 100 ms so the old session cannot release the new foreground before identity delivery. |
